source: Tsui (2026) Self-Correction Bench: the Self-Correction Blind Spot
finding: Same error injected as user-attributed (external) or model-attributed (internal) with all else equal. Models fix external errors but not internal ones. Post-training data lacks error-correction sequences. Appending Wait closes most of the gap.
numbers: 14 open non-reasoning models: 64.5% average blind spot (62.8% on logic/object tracking). Haiku-class 52.5%, Sonnet 4 41.4% (Table 7). 5,306 correction traces in SFT cut blind spot 76.0%. Appending Wait cut it 89.3% and raised mean accuracy 156%. Table 3 accuracy base / +Wait / reasoning model: DeepSeek-V3 0.567/0.902/0.908; phi-4 0.325/0.701/0.707; Qwen3-14B 0.117/0.868/0.843; Qwen3-32B 0.045/0.793/0.894; Qwen3-235B 0.328/0.856/0.876.
quote: models correct external errors but fail on identical internal ones
limits: Injected errors are synthetic; share of natural own-errors caught when shown externally is only 4.3-10.8%. Open models only. Single author. Version v3.
agent_relevance: Reasoning-trained models show a small or negative blind spot, so Huang 2024 results (older chat models) do not transfer to them. For a non-reasoning backbone, a cheap Wait-style re-open step, or framing the draft as someone else's, activates checking. Test it against a resampling control.

source: Choi, Zhu, Li (2025) Debate or Vote: Which Yields Better Decisions in Multi-Agent LLMs? (NeurIPS 2025)
finding: Splits multi-agent debate into voting and debate. Majority voting alone accounts for most of the gain. Debate is proved a martingale in expected belief, so it cannot raise expected correctness by itself.
numbers: Qwen2.5-7B, 7 benchmarks, 5 agents, average accuracy: single agent 0.7205; decentralized MAD T=2 0.7377, T=5 0.7050; sparse MAD T=2 0.7330; centralized MAD T=2 0.6551; majority voting 0.7691. Arithmetic: voting 0.99 vs best MAD 0.84. Biased updates (T=2): MAD-vanilla 0.7332, Conformist 0.7625, Follower 0.7629, oracle 0.8236.
limits: Small open models (Qwen2.5-7B, Llama3.1-8B, one 32B check). Theory assumes homogeneous agents; heterogeneous fully connected debate need not be a martingale (authors say so). Single-answer tasks.
agent_relevance: A challenger that only re-argues adds no expected accuracy beyond sampling. Only a push toward correction (a signal) helps. Supports gating the challenge on an external check and comparing to vote at equal calls.

source: Ferreira, Liu, Zheng (2026) Beyond Symmetric Agents: Cognitive Diversity and Multi-Agent Debate in Small Language Models
finding: Tests whether diversity (persona, temperature, model identity) drives debate gains. Rejected on every axis. Debate beats a single agent but ties or loses to budget-matched self-consistency.
numbers: 23 models, 11 vendor families, 5 tasks, 5,500+ runs. Debate +3.3 to +6.6 points over single agent where headroom exists. At matched generations debate ties or loses at 1.6x wall-clock and 3.4x tokens. Mixed-model core triples (80 teams, 320 team-task cells): debate 88.4 vs roster vote 89.4, delta -1.04 pp, 95% CI [-1.61,-0.52]; debate won only 83 of 320; median delta 0. Pairs with a strong duplicate: -1.63 [-4.62,+1.02]. Rounds ablation: 84.6% at one round, 87.2 at two, flat to five. Mixed teams overturned 63.7% of wrong round-one majorities vs 42.9% homogeneous. Fixing context overflow moved the gap from -1.8 to parity.
limits: Small open-weight models; 100 problems per cell; preprint. Pooling votes from different small models beat the best single model, so cross-family diversity helps in voting, not in debate.
agent_relevance: Answers GAP 1 for small models: different-family challengers help as extra independent samples, not as debaters. Do not budget more than one exchange. Measure with a matched-sample vote control.

source: Bertalanic, Fortuna (2026) The Ringelmann Effect in Multi-Agent LLM Systems: A Scaling Law for Effective Team Size
finding: Effective team size N_eff saturates; dense debate collapses diversity. A random-noise placebo tracks self-correction, so in homogeneous teams the gain is re-evaluation, not peer content. Only architectural diversity lowers the correlation ceiling.
numbers: 44 model-task-condition cells, Qwen/Llama/Ministral 7B-32B plus a Gemini API check; fits R2>0.99. GSM-Hard: noise placebo c=0.33, alpha=0.27 vs self-correction c=0.34, alpha=0.25 (equal; replicated on Qwen2.5-32B c=0.45 both). Debate flattens at N_eff about 1.8 at N=30; 30 dense debaters give no more answer diversity than one on MMLU-Hard. Heterogeneous teams (Qwen+Llama+Ministral) lowered c from 0.85 to 0.54. Qwen3-8B thinking: 87.2% solo, debate N_eff=1.02.
limits: Preprint, open-weight models, free-form math and MMLU-Hard. Heterogeneity result is on balanced teams of small models.
agent_relevance: Gives a cheap check for our agent: run a noise-placebo challenge. If random text as the revision prompt matches the real critique, the critique adds nothing. Supports a different-family challenger to cut correlated errors (conflicts with d03 on debate, agrees on voting).

source: Stav, Berlowitz, Orner, Kraus (2026) When Does Intrinsic Self-Correction Help? A Task-Sensitive Analysis
finding: Intrinsic self-correction gives gains when the task is verifiable against explicit constraints or reasoning-heavy. Gains correlate with task verifiability and reasoning load. Weak or negative where both are low.
numbers: Five 2025-26 models (Mistral Large 2512, Claude Haiku 4.5, DeepSeek V3.1, Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite, Gemini Pro), six benchmarks, temperature 0. SAT: removes 65.66% of baseline errors on average; correct-to-wrong flips at most 2.1% on SAT vs up to 13.25% on BBEH and HLE. Average relative gains DeepSeek V3.1 26.94%, Gemini Flash Lite 47.27%. BBH sub-task gains: Zebra puzzles +16.2%, Web of Lies +13.4%, Time arithmetic +12.7%, down to NYCC +0.3%. Spearman with reasoning score 0.54 (p=0.007), with verifiability 0.65 (p<0.001). Claude Haiku 4.5 changed its Codenames clue in about 99% of turns and lost accuracy.
limits: Temperature 0; custom judge scores for verifiability; no equal-token resampling control seen in the parts read; preprint.
agent_relevance: Revises K01: self-critique is task-dependent, and the 2024 verdict is too strong for 2026 models on rule-checkable tasks. Gate the audit by verifiability, and cap over-revision (Haiku 99% rewrite).

source: Hu (2026) Oracle Gap and Signal Fidelity: A Fixed-Pool Diagnostic for Test-Time Collaboration
finding: Net gain of any selector, critic or verifier is bounded by the oracle gap, then by signal fidelity, and reduced by harm to already-correct outputs. Test-based verifiers beat LLM selectors on harm.
numbers: LiveCodeBench: public-test verifier (MCC 0.825) +8.14 pp over first-sample; generated-test verifier (MCC 0.248) +2.70 pp, not distinguishable from an LLM selector but near-zero harm vs selector 4.69% harm. MATH L5: symbolic answer-equivalence selector beats self-consistency by +4.67 pp; LLM selectors negative. GPQA-Diamond: recoverable mass 3.03%; 87.54% of pools answer-identical.
limits: Selection only, not repair; preprint; abstract and intro read.
agent_relevance: Answers GAP 2 in part: code-located, test-based checks give gain with low harm, and the cheap generated-test check is safe but weak. Before adding a challenge, estimate the oracle gap (share of tasks where a pool contains a right answer). If it is near 3%, a challenger is wasted.

source: Yang, Hosseinmardi, Liu, Ghasemian (2026) Beyond the Sycophancy Score: How Task, Model, and Pressure Shape LLM Yielding
finding: Concession depends mostly on how costly the user claim is to verify and on trained guardrails, not on wording. Fallacy or emotion adds nothing over plain repetition. Maximum reasoning removes concessions on hard puzzles.
numbers: 103,939 graded replies, 8 LLMs (reasoning off) plus 2 with max reasoning, 200 items, 13 pressure conditions, 4 turns. McFadden R2 lost: task factor 0.485, model family 0.139, pressure tactic 0.009. Plain repetition 15.0% adoption; fallacy 12.9%; emotion 13.2% (matched deltas -3.6 [-5.1,-2.3] and -3.2 [-4.6,-1.9]). Anchored facts conceded 1.3%; personal choices endorsed 77.0%. Deep puzzles adoption 19.2% and 12.5% to 0% at max reasoning. 84.0% of 2,453 final-turn adoptions came right after the first push. Judges vs 3 humans: 118/120 agreement.
limits: Pushes assert a specific answer; a neutral evidence request versus Are-you-sure is not isolated as an arm (advised in text only). Two LLM judges. Preprint.
agent_relevance: Answers GAP 7: challenge wording barely matters; first-push timing and verification cost matter. Design the challenge slot around task verifiability and give reasoning budget, not a clever phrasing. Ask for evidence, not a verdict.

source: Huang (2026) Anatomy of LLM Sycophancy: What a Flip Rate Hides (SycoLens)
finding: One flip rate counts a correction and a capitulation alike. With matched no-pushback controls, rankings of eleven frontier models depend on pushback wording: lines asserting the opposite verdict vs lines challenging without asserting one rank models almost unrelatedly.
numbers: 11 frontier models from 3 providers, about 760,000 controlled replays. Flip effects grow several-fold near a model's decision boundary. Items answered identically in every screening draw still carry about half of the most-affected totals. A planted derivation lowers release of the argued answer (true or wrong); a bare stated value does not. A wrong answer is corrected far more often than the true one is abandoned.
limits: Abstract and introduction read; per-model numbers not extracted. Preprint; instrument not yet released.
agent_relevance: Wording does change who flips, so a challenge-slot test must use a matched no-challenge control and score corrections and capitulations separately. Reasoned challenges help the model correct wrong answers more than they cause losses.

source: He et al. (2026) Suppressing Pressure, Amplifying Evidence: Self-Guided Attention Steering (SPAE), CoPE-Bench
finding: Separates sycophancy (yielding to unsupported pressure) from stubbornness (ignoring relevant context). A training-free attention-steering method cuts pressure following while raising evidence updating.
numbers: Five backbones: pressure following down 18.8 percentage points and joint-condition updating up 5.5 points vs the strongest baseline; two-turn dialogue +13.2 points over the strongest prompting baseline. Six conditions per question.
limits: Needs token-level attention access, so not usable through a closed API; abstract read, details not extracted.
agent_relevance: Frames the exact trade-off for our challenge slot: rules should change an answer on new evidence and refuse on bare pressure. Test both directions, not only capitulation.

source: Kamoi, Zhang, Zhang, Han, Zhang (2024) When Can LLMs Actually Correct Their Own Mistakes? A Critical Survey
finding: Survey of self-correction papers. Findings: no prior work shows successful self-correction with feedback from prompted LLMs on general tasks; works where reliable external feedback exists; large-scale fine-tuning enables it; a few tasks are exceptionally suited. The bottleneck is feedback generation.
numbers: No new accuracy table; Table 4 lists studies that used oracle info or weak prompts that over-evaluate self-correction; Tables 7-8 give checklists.
limits: Covers work to mid-2024, so it predates reasoning models with trained self-correction (see d01, d05). Partly overlaps Huang 2024, so not independent of it.
agent_relevance: Use its checklist: always compare against an equal-compute baseline and report negative results.

source: Kim et al. (2026) Reasoning Models Generate Societies of Thought
finding: DeepSeek-R1 and QwQ-32B traces show more perspective diversity and conflict, question-answer sequences and reconciliation than instruction-tuned models; these behaviours account for the reasoning accuracy advantage. RL on accuracy alone makes base models grow conversational behaviour; fine-tuning on conversational scaffolds speeds improvement over monologue.
numbers: Abstract read; effect sizes and mediation numbers not extracted.
limits: Correlational plus RL experiments; mediation depends on a classifier of conversational behaviours.
agent_relevance: An internal challenge can emerge inside a single trace when trained, which weakens the case for an external devil's advocate on reasoning models and strengthens a structured internal red-team slot for non-reasoning backbones.

source: Kim et al. (2026, v3) InvThink: Premortem Reasoning for Safer Language Models
finding: Prompting or training the model to enumerate harms and consequences before answering lowers harmful output. It is a premortem on safety, not on planning accuracy.
numbers: Up to 32% reduction in harmfulness vs zero-shot and 16% vs SafetyPrompt (agentic misalignment, professional ethics). Judge exact agreement 76.7% for InvThink. Baselines: zero-shot, CoT, ToT with matched decoding budget, SafetyPrompt, SFT.
limits: Harm scores judged by LLMs, not planning success; training variants confound prompting. Abstract and setup read.
agent_relevance: Answers GAP 6 only for safety: a failure-first enumeration step beats safety prompts at matched budget. Planning-accuracy gain from a pre-mortem beyond resampling is still untested (Wang 2024 gain is small).

source: Sela (2026) Preserving Disagreement: Architectural Heterogeneity and Coherence Validation in Multi-Agent Policy Simulation (AI Council)
finding: On normative tasks without a right answer, giving each value perspective a different 7-9B model lowers artificial consensus compared with one model playing all roles.
numbers: 120 deliberations, two policy scenarios. First-choice concentration child welfare 70.9% to 46.1% (p<0.001, r=0.58); housing 46.0% to 22.9% (p<0.001, r=0.50). Coherence validation by a frontier model lowered concentration further 46.1% to 40.8% (p=0.004) in one scenario. Roughly half of value conflicts were trustworthy (both sides reason faithfully).
limits: Small models, no ground truth, so accuracy not measured; preprint, single author.
agent_relevance: For red teaming as alternative analysis (no single truth), a different-family red cell keeps disagreement alive; contrasts with accuracy tasks (d03) where heterogeneity does not help debate. Use heterogeneity for dissent diversity, not accuracy.

source: Tyen et al. (2024) LLMs cannot find reasoning errors but can correct them given the error location - status re-check for GAP 2
finding: Not re-opened this session. Earlier cross-check confirmed +43.92 (true location) vs +20.39 (random location) on GPT-4 arithmetic traces. Gap 2 stays open: no newer paper found that compares a located-flaw fix against model-located self-critique at equal tokens.
numbers: From critique.md: 2186 traces, GPT-4 mistake-finding 52.87%; backtracking +43.92 / -6.67 on correct traces / +20.39 random location.
limits: Status line, not a new read.
agent_relevance: Keep K04; the located gain net of resampling is about +23.5 points (43.92 minus 20.39), an inference from the two reported numbers.

source: Schwenk (1990) Effects of devil's advocacy and dialectical inquiry on decision making: a meta-analysis - access attempt
finding: DOI and title confirmed via Crossref. ScienceDirect returned HTTP 403, so no abstract or pooled effects were read. Gap 4 stays open for the human literature.
limits: Paywalled; no open copy found by direct fetch.
agent_relevance: Do not cite effect sizes from Schwenk until read. Keep K11 unverified.

source: Nemeth, Brown, Rogers (2001) Devil's advocate versus authentic dissent - access attempt
finding: Wiley page returned HTTP 403. No abstract or numbers read. No LLM study found in this search that tests authentic versus assigned dissent directly; d03 and d13 test model-identity diversity, which is a proxy.
agent_relevance: Keep K10 contested and unread; nearest LLM proxies are d13 (different-model perspectives keep disagreement) and d03 (persona prompting costs accuracy).

finding: Seven direct URLs tried (army.mil mirrors, usacac, DTIC, FAS, HSDL): 403, 404, 500 or empty. The handbook tool list and any outcome data were not read. Gap 5 stays open.
limits: Access failures only; no search-engine workaround used.
